sourceLongSummaries: The party finishes discussing the Dreamer notebook's conflation of dreams and souls before the session recap returns them to Kallipseis's fungal greenhouse. After restating their appearances and motives, they debate whether they owe anything to Hulda or Lord Endless Ending, question Menestheus about the order and its absent leader, and consider the risk that taking the glass key could release the prisoner. They conclude that the key is still their best route out, but intend to remove it without opening the prisoner's door, and leave Kallipseis to continue work on her fungal golem.

After crossing a parlor, the party enters a lecture hall whose blackboard diagrams wind-dispersed plants and whose enormous black painting conceals a star field, a tear in the universe, and the textured shape of a sprouting seed. Tarek also finds The Shape of Discovery, a treatise linking curiosity, greed, chance, and possibility, while the group realizes that Alden matched Kallipseis's description of an infected person. Menestheus identifies the painted seed crossing between worlds as exactly the kind of breach his order guarded against. In the next clockworks workshop, Tarek takes a portable space-time clock whose changing numbers track the prison's position, and the party reaches another listening station.

The notebook titled Thirst describes the speaker filling empty heads with its children and being helped to find the person who can free it. The party interprets the children as the fungal infection, suspects the prisoner manipulated Alden and the false-looking deed that brought them here, and resolves not to free it. When Kaito takes the listener's role, he hears the prisoner claim it is full of dreams, can read the party, and sees both the moving exit and a hole large enough for its children. The group moves into an animal experimentation lab filled with cages, restraints, dead animals, an infected ant colony, and humanoid remains; as they approach the exit, a hand pulls Menestheus out of sight.

After Menestheus is seized, the table establishes the animal-lab battlefield and the party begins its rescue. Edric rages, crosses the obstructing tables, and hammers the mushroom man holding Menestheus; Kaito follows with Dissonant Whispers, while Tarek and Ayveen position for ranged and melee support. As Tarek approaches, the nearby corpse opens its eyes and rises, looking nearly identical to Alden. The party damages both infected bodies, but the opening exchange ends as the newly awakened corpse stands and reaches for Tarek.

The awakened mushroom man lashes out with elongated fingers, briefly grapples Tarek, and exposes multiple mouths in its chest while the other feeds Menestheus toward them. Ayveen's Silvery Barbs reduces the attack, Txarro becomes a tiger, and the party focuses down the first body before turning on Menestheus's captor. The surviving creature pulls Menestheus into its chest, dropping him to zero hit points and inflicting a failed death save, but Txarro restores him with Cure Wounds. Edric finally crushes the last mushroom man's head; its death releases a cloud of seeds that Txarro inhales, after which the party burns both bodies as they flare like dry straw.

After further healing restores Menestheus, the party crosses a dead plant greenhouse and a picked-over armory while questioning what the complex was built to do. A close examination finds his wounds apparently healed but reveals white filamentous growth inside his mouth; Tarek quietly warns Txarro, and they decide not to tell Menestheus until they know how to help him. The group continues through an unfinished planar orrery and a corridor of offices. Thalestria's sealed office has no visible lock, and even Edric's enraged attempts cannot force the door, which he accepts as a warning from the gods before the party moves on.

In the map library, Menestheus describes other Arithrimos Lamperum facilities and an indefinitely confined creature that perceived its whole life at once and served as an augury. The party then passes through a fabrication lab into room 25, where the prisoner loops statements addressed to Hulda and declares that Hulda is bringing five friends who are outside its room and can hear it now. One door from the prisoner, they enter room 26, a massive library whose shelves include chained books. A human-sized porcelain and clockwork torso anchored to a desk raises its head, opens its eyes, and studies the party, providing the session's cliffhanger before the table briefly debriefs.

sourceEntries.title: Mushroom Men Defeated
sourceEntries.boundaryReason: The mushroom men counterattack, nearly kill Menestheus, and are destroyed by the party; the combat scene closes when their remains are burned.
sourceEntries.shortSummary: The mushroom men nearly kill Menestheus, but the party destroys both infected bodies and burns their remains.
sourceEntries.longSummary: The awakened mushroom man lashes out with elongated fingers, briefly grapples Tarek, and exposes multiple mouths in its chest while the other feeds Menestheus toward them. Ayveen's Silvery Barbs reduces the attack, Txarro becomes a tiger, and the party focuses down the first body before turning on Menestheus's captor. The surviving creature pulls Menestheus into its chest, dropping him to zero hit points and inflicting a failed death save, but Txarro restores him with Cure Wounds. Edric finally crushes the last mushroom man's head; its death releases a cloud of seeds that Txarro inhales, after which the party burns both bodies as they flare like dry straw.

recapBlocks.title: Infection and Locked Offices
sourceShortSummaries: Tarek discovers fungal growth inside the healed Menestheus, and the party presses through more workrooms before failing to break into Thalestria's office.
sourceLongSummaries: After further healing restores Menestheus, the party crosses a dead plant greenhouse and a picked-over armory while questioning what the complex was built to do. A close examination finds his wounds apparently healed but reveals white filamentous growth inside his mouth; Tarek quietly warns Txarro, and they decide not to tell Menestheus until they know how to help him. The group continues through an unfinished planar orrery and a corridor of offices. Thalestria's sealed office has no visible lock, and even Edric's enraged attempts cannot force the door, which he accepts as a warning from the gods before the party moves on.

recapBlocks.title: The Prisoner Speaks
sourceShortSummaries: The prisoner addresses Hulda and her five friends through a listening station, and the session ends when a clockwork figure awakens in the final library before the prisoner's door.
sourceLongSummaries: In the map library, Menestheus describes other Arithrimos Lamperum facilities and an indefinitely confined creature that perceived its whole life at once and served as an augury. The party then passes through a fabrication lab into room 25, where the prisoner loops statements addressed to Hulda and declares that Hulda is bringing five friends who are outside its room and can hear it now. One door from the prisoner, they enter room 26, a massive library whose shelves include chained books. A human-sized porcelain and clockwork torso anchored to a desk raises its head, opens its eyes, and studies the party, providing the session's cliffhanger before the table briefly debriefs.
